newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest bourse links voting rights to turnover.
newsitem.headline: Budapest bourse links voting rights to turnover.

text.p: The annual general meeting of the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) has approved a change in voting rights, linking them to turnover in each of its three sections, BSE officials said on Friday.

"Voting rights (of the bourse members) will be established according to turnover," Kalman Debreceni, member of the bourse council, who chaired this year's annual general meeting, told a news conference.

He added that in each of the bourse's three sections -- government bonds, stocks and futures section -- a medium turnover range will be established, and bourse members falling in that bracket will be entitled to five votes.
Votes per member, calculated based on a progressive formula, can reach a maximum 10 or a minimum one, he said.
So far, the BSE had a one member, one vote policy.
The decision made at the annual general meeting still requires approval by the State Money and Capital Market Supervision (APTF), he said.
In 1996, the top three bourse members by stock turnover were ING Baring Securities, Creditanstalt Securities and CS First Boston.
In terms of government bonds turnover, ING Baring Securities, OTP Securities and Creditanstalt Securities headed the list last year.
In the ranking by 1996 securities turnover, ING Baring Securities, Creditanstalt Securities and OTP Securities were the top three BSE members.
